target: Nu komt de aap uit de mouw, hij had het al die tijd geweten.
english: Now the cat's out of the bag–he had known it all along.
tip: 'De aap komt uit de mouw' means the hidden truth or real motive finally comes out. Nu komt de aap uit de mouw.

target: Wij zijn begonnen met het opruimen van de zolder.
english: We started cleaning up the attic.
tip: Put 'het' before an infinitive to turn a verb into a noun: het opruimen (the cleaning-up), so begonnen met het opruimen means started the tidying.

target: Wij kregen te horen dat de vlucht was geannuleerd.
english: We were told that the flight had been cancelled.
tip: 'krijgen te horen' literally means to get to hear, the Dutch way of saying to be told: kregen te horen dat (were told that).

target: Hij weet niet hoe de vork in de steel zit.
english: He doesn't know how things really are.
tip: hoe de vork in de steel zit literally means how the fork sits in its handle, and stands for how things really are.

target: Zij slaagt erin om alles op tijd klaar te krijgen.
english: She manages to get everything ready on time.
tip: slagen in becomes erin slagen, where er points ahead to what you succeed in: Zij slaagt erin om alles klaar te krijgen = she manages to get it done.

target: Zij is te moe om nog langer door te werken.
english: She is too tired to continue working any longer.
tip: Separable verbs split around te: doorwerken becomes door te werken. Zij is te moe om nog langer door te werken.

target: Zij vangt twee vliegen in een klap met dit plan.
english: She kills two birds with one stone with this plan.
tip: The Dutch equivalent of two birds with one stone is two flies in one swat: Zij vangt twee vliegen in een klap.

target: Hij kwam naar Nederland om te studeren.
english: He came to the Netherlands to study.
tip: om te plus an infinitive marks purpose, in order to: om te studeren = in order to study.

target: Zij stelt het op prijs als je niet om de hete brij draait.
english: She appreciates it if you don't beat around the bush.
tip: om de hete brij draaien literally means to circle around the hot porridge, and means to beat around the bush.

target: Tot morgen, slaap lekker!
english: Until tomorrow, sleep well!
tip: 'lekker' isn't only about taste. In 'slaap lekker' it means pleasantly or well, the usual Dutch way to say good night.

target: Hallo, leuk je te ontmoeten!
english: Hello, nice to meet you!
tip: 'Leuk je te ontmoeten' – 'om' is often omitted in casual speech before 'te' + infinitive.

target: De buurman klaagde dat de muziek te hard stond.
english: The neighbor complained that the music was too loud.
tip: For sound, 'hard' means loud, not difficult. So 'de muziek stond te hard' says the music was too loud.

target: Nergens in de stad vind je betere koffie dan hier.
english: Nowhere in the city will you find better coffee than here.
tip: Starting with 'Nergens' flips subject and verb: it becomes 'vind je', not 'je vindt', keeping the verb in second place.

target: Ik snap er niks van, eerlijk gezegd.
english: I don't understand any of it, honestly.
tip: 'snappen van' wraps around 'er': 'ik snap er niks van' = I understand nothing of it. 'er ... van' points to the topic.

target: Hij ontkende dat hij de fout had gemaakt.
english: He denied that he had made the mistake.
tip: After 'dat', Dutch pushes the verbs to the end: 'dat hij de fout had gemaakt', not 'dat hij had de fout gemaakt'.

target: Hij fluisterde haar in het oor dat hij van haar hield.
english: He whispered in her ear that he loved her.
tip: 'houden' needs 'van' to mean love: 'hij hield van haar' = he loved her. Without 'van' it means to keep or hold.

target: Namens het bestuur wil ik u hartelijk danken voor uw bijdrage.
english: On behalf of the board, I would like to thank you warmly for your contribution.
tip: 'Namens' is formal for 'on behalf of'.

target: Het centraal station is goed bereikbaar met zowel de bus als de tram.
english: The central station is easily accessible by both bus and tram.
tip: 'zowel ... als' pairs two items as both and: 'zowel de bus als de tram' = both the bus and the tram.

target: Prettige feestdagen!
english: Happy holidays!
tip: 'Prettige' – adjective before a de-word gets -e ending: 'prettige feestdagen'.

target: Hoi, alles goed met je?
english: Hi, everything okay with you?
tip: 'Alles goed met je?' – a casual check-in. Verb 'gaat' is dropped in informal Dutch.

target: Ik ga zo weg, tot morgen!
english: I'm leaving soon, see you tomorrow!
tip: 'Zo' means 'soon' in this context – very casual time indicator.

target: Hij staat met zijn mond vol tanden van verbazing.
english: He is lost for words with amazement.
tip: met de mond vol tanden staan literally means to stand with your mouth full of teeth, and means to be lost for words.

target: Gelieve uw reactie schriftelijk in te dienen.
english: Please submit your response in writing.
tip: 'Gelieve' is extremely formal – used in legal and bureaucratic contexts only.

target: De schoonmoeder komt zondag op de koffie.
english: The mother-in-law is coming for coffee on Sunday.
tip: 'Schoonmoeder' = schoon (clean/in-law) + moeder – 'schoon-' means 'in-law' in family terms.

target: Gaarne ontvang ik uw bevestiging per omgaande.
english: I would like to receive your confirmation by return.
tip: 'Gaarne' is extremely formal for 'graag' – only in written business Dutch.

target: Ik wil u erop wijzen dat de regels zijn gewijzigd.
english: I wish to point out to you that the rules have been changed.
tip: 'Erop wijzen' is formal; informally you'd say 'even zeggen dat'.

target: Wij zitten met de handen in het haar over dit probleem.
english: We are at our wits' end about this problem.
tip: met de handen in het haar zitten literally means to sit with your hands in your hair, and means to be at your wits end.

target: Aangehecht treft u de benodigde documenten aan.
english: Please find the required documents attached.
tip: 'Aangehecht' is formal email language – 'attached herewith'.

target: Het lammetje springt vrolijk in de wei.
english: The little lamb jumps happily in the meadow.
tip: Diminutive -etje: after short vowel + m: 'lam' → 'lammetje'.

target: Voorts wil ik u eraan herinneren dat de deadline nadert.
english: Furthermore, I would like to remind you that the deadline is approaching.
tip: 'Voorts' is extremely formal for 'verder' or 'ook'.
